renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Short words. Concrete images. No jargon, no Sanskrit terms, no meta-commentary.

paragraphs.text: Bow to the world-shaped one, past the world — to the always-shining god, the self with power that never ends.
You, and only you. Me, and only me. You are, and I am not at all. You-and-me together? Nothing there — so bow, and bow again.
I looked for you inside my body, forever — you as me, but me never found. Whatever gets seen — that's you, that.
Your fan says he really knows your shape — now, again: he saw you as himself, so to you bows, to me bows.
How clever is going, what should get done, and how, from the ground up? Yours is magic-nature stuff — so with what, in what, from where does it melt away?
Me, you. You, me. So there's no two-ness of us anywhere. The only reason split stays standing is wanting to grab samādhi.
You, me, and all that — so endless, always in you, they find no slot. So where do words come from — the world?
Enough with the difference chatter. Chew the sap of wanting you till there's no juice left — everything's one, it's cool — though even saying so feels shy.
When your shape puffs up — you, me, the whole world. When it sucks back in — no you, no me, no world, for real.
Waking, dreaming, deep sleep and the rest — hold them like your own sunbeams. You shine because you feel like it, like an actor — and still no parts, really true.
